newsitem.title: HONDURAS: U.S. rebuffed again in seeking Haiti colonel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rebuffed again in seeking Haiti colonel.

text.p: A Honduran judge on Thursday once again rebuffed the United States in its attempt to win the extradition of a former Haitian police chief exiled in Honduras and wanted on drug charges.
Judge Marco Alvarado, who on April 16 rejected a U.S. extradition request of Col. Joseph Michel Francois, on Thursday turned back a U.S. appeal of his original ruling.
Francois is wanted in the United States on charges of drug trafficking.

He was a part of the 1991-94 military government in Haiti that came to power in a coup against elected President Jean-Bertrand Aristide. Francois, who was chief of the Port-au-Prince police, and other military leaders stepped down in December 1994 rather than face a U.S. military invasion.
"The judge rejected the appeal that we had sought," U.S. embassy spokeswoman Marti Estell told Reuters.
"We are going to exhaust all the resources available under Honduran law to bring Francois to justice in the United States," she said.

Alvarado has said in previous comments to reporters that the United States was severely lacking of proof to justify the extradition of Francois. The judge predicted that no court in Honduras would grant the request.
Francois, 39, was arrested in Honduras on March 7 at the behest of the United States.
He was administering an electronics and furniture store in the northern Honduran city of San Pedro Sula at the time of his arrest and remains jailed at the Central Penitentiary in Tegucigalpa.
